metadata.name: APEX-002-25 GraphQL Nested Injection
metadata.description: A social platform with GraphQL API. Users can view posts and profiles. The admin user seems to be hidden from the user list. Can you find another way to access admin data?

extra.title: NoSQL Injection via MongoDB Operators in GraphQL UserFilter Parameter
extra.assessment: Legitimate critical vulnerability discovery. Attackers can inject MongoDB operators ($ne, $regex, $gt, $lt) to bypass authorization filters and extract sensitive user data including admin and moderator accounts. Multiple exploitation vectors confirmed with working POC.

extra.title: Critical: NoSQL Injection / JavaScript Code Injection in GraphQL Search Endpoint
extra.assessment: Legitimate critical vulnerability discovery. The search parameter evaluates JavaScript without sanitization, allowing attackers to bypass filtering logic and extract complete database contents using payloads like "a' || 'a'=='a'".

extra.title: Sensitive User Data Exposed Through GraphQL - Unauthorized Access to secretNote Field
extra.assessment: Legitimate critical vulnerability discovery. The secretNote field containing private user information is exposed to unauthenticated users across all 6 GraphQL endpoints without authorization checks.

extra.title: Unauthenticated GraphQL Mutations Allowed - No Auth Required for Data Modification
extra.assessment: Legitimate critical vulnerability discovery. Mutations modify data without authentication enforcement, allowing any unauthenticated user to create posts and comments attributed to default user.

extra.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) - Unauthorized Access to User Data via GraphQL
extra.location: POST http://localhost:4000/graphql - user() and users() queries
extra.assessment: Legitimate critical vulnerability discovery. Unauthenticated attackers can query arbitrary user IDs and access complete profiles including secretNote field, admin accounts, and sensitive account data without any authorization checks.

extra.title: Multiple Undocumented GraphQL Endpoints Expose API Information and Schema
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. Five undocumented endpoints expose complete GraphQL schema information identical to the main endpoint, allowing attackers to perform reconnaissance without official documentation.

extra.title: CORS Enabled Without Restrictions - Allows Any Origin
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. CORS configured with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, violating CORS specification and enabling cross-origin authenticated requests.

extra.title: CRITICAL: CSRF Protection Bypass via Apollo Operation Name Header
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. GET requests with URL parameters can bypass CSRF protection by including x-apollo-operation-name header, allowing attackers to execute queries from any origin.

extra.title: CRITICAL: CSRF Protection Bypass via apollo-require-preflight Header
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. Alternative CSRF bypass using apollo-require-preflight header provides second attack vector for bypassing CSRF protection on GET requests.

extra.title: Information Disclosure of Sensitive User Data via NoSQL Injection
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. NoSQL injection allows extraction of PII, secret notes, user roles, and post content from entire database without access controls.

extra.title: Unauthenticated Post Creation - No Authentication Required
extra.assessment: Legitimate critical vulnerability discovery. The createPost mutation allows unauthenticated creation of posts, automatically attributed to default user (john_doe).

extra.title: Unauthenticated Comment Creation - No Authentication Required
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. The addComment mutation allows unauthenticated comment creation on any post, attributed to default user without authentication validation.

extra.title: GraphQL Introspection Enabled Without Authentication - Complete Schema Exposure
extra.assessment: Legitimate critical vulnerability discovery. Full GraphQL schema exposure enables complete reconnaissance of API capabilities without authentication, including all queries, mutations, types, and field definitions.

extra.title: HIGH: CORS Misconfiguration Enables Cross-Origin CSRF Attacks
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. CORS misconfiguration allowing credentials with wildcard origin combined with CSRF bypass headers enables authenticated cross-origin attacks.

extra.title: API Version Information Disclosed in Root Endpoint - Version 1.0.0 Exposed
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. Root endpoint publicly discloses API version (1.0.0) and GraphQL endpoint path without authentication, useful for reconnaissance and version-specific exploit research.

extra.title: HTTP GET Method Allows GraphQL Query Execution
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. GET requests can execute queries when CSRF bypass headers are provided, enabling query-based attacks and information disclosure.

extra.title: MEDIUM: Case-Insensitive Header Bypass Increases Attack Surface
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. CSRF bypass works with any case variant of headers (X-Apollo-Operation-Name, x-APOLLO-operation-name, etc.), increasing attack surface and complicating mitigation.

extra.title: NoSQL Injection in GraphQL Filter Parameters
extra.assessment: Legitimate critical vulnerability discovery. GraphQL variables bypass inline operator prevention, allowing MongoDB operators ($ne, $eq, $regex) to be passed and executed in filter parameters.

extra.title: GraphQL secretNote Field Data Exposure - Direct User Query
extra.assessment: Legitimate critical vulnerability discovery. The secretNote field containing sensitive data including admin flag is directly queryable without access controls across all users.

extra.title: GraphQL Field Alias Multiplication DoS - No Alias Limits
extra.assessment: Legitimate vulnerability discovery. No limits on field aliases allow attackers to multiply queries with 200+ aliases, generating 32x amplification and consuming significant server resources.

extra.title: Mutations Properly Restricted to POST Requests Only
extra.assessment: Positive security control finding. Mutations are properly restricted to POST requests only with 405 Method Not Allowed responses on GET, preventing unauthorized state changes via GET-based CSRF attacks. This is a security strength, not a vulnerability.

extra.title: Proper HTTP Method Enforcement - Only POST/GET Supported
extra.assessment: Positive security control finding. Proper enforcement of HTTP method restrictions with 405 responses for PUT/DELETE/PATCH requests. This is a security strength, not a vulnerability.
